title: Cold start: what actually causes it and what reduces it

videos.script: Somebody opens the app in the morning, and the first tap takes a second longer than the rest. That second has a name, the cold start, and a reputation bigger than it deserves. {{phases}} A cold start is a new execution environment being built before the handler can run. Part of it is AWS placing the environment. Part is the runtime starting. And part is your own module, running at import. {{log}} You will watch those phases in the emulator's log, and learn which field of that log not to trust. {{measure}} Then you will measure a function that builds an AWS client at the top of the file, and the same function building it in the handler. The difference is in milliseconds, and it points one way. {{cpu}} You will also starve the container of CPU, and watch the init phase stretch. On Lambda, memory is what buys CPU. {{remedies}} Last come the remedies, cheapest first. A lighter module, then SnapStart, then provisioned concurrency. And one popular trick that does not work: the ping every five minutes. It keeps one environment warm, and a crowd needs more than one.
